Universe as Memory Substrate

Information Conservation & Black Holes

If information is conserved (unitary quantum mechanics), the universe acts as a memory substrate that never truly forgets.

Quantum unitarity implies information is never destroyed: interactions spread and scramble correlations rather than erase them. The black hole information paradox sharpened this point: Hawking radiation looked thermal, but holography (Bekenstein bound, AdS/CFT) and modern island calculations restore a unitary Page curve. In this view, the universe itself is a memory substrate whose present state encodes all past interactions — though practical recovery is typically impossible due to extreme scrambling and decoherence.
